Excel Pivot Table – Step-by-Step Guide
Create, format, align, filter and move fields in a Pivot Table.
📚 Detailed Pivot Table Guide
Follow the screenshots step-by-step to create and format your Pivot Table.
1

Step 1 – Start with Your Data

Begin with a simple data table containing fields such as Name, Type, Other and Quantity. Make sure the column headers are clear and the data is arranged in rows.

2

Step 2 – Insert a Pivot Table

Click inside the source data, go to Insert → PivotTable, and confirm the PivotTable location. Excel opens the PivotTable Fields pane on the right.

3

Step 3 – Add Fields to Rows

In the PivotTable Fields pane, select fields such as Name, Type and Other. These fields are placed in the Rows area and create the row structure of the Pivot Table.

4

Step 4 – Add Quantity to Values

Select Quantity so it goes into the Values area. Excel automatically summarizes the numbers, for example as Sum of Quantity.

5

Step 5 – Open Report Layout

Go to the Design tab, click Report Layout, and choose the layout option you need. The menu also contains Repeat All Item Labels.

6

Step 6 – Show the Pivot Table in Tabular Form

Choose Report Layout → Show in Tabular Form. This displays the row fields in separate columns, making the Pivot Table easier to read and work with.

7

Step 7 – Repeat All Item Labels

If some row labels appear blank, open Report Layout again and select Repeat All Item Labels. Excel repeats the parent label on each applicable row.

8

Step 8 – Apply a Filter

Move a field such as Name into the Filters area. Click the filter drop-down and select the value you want, such as A, to show only matching records.

9

Step 9 – Move a Field to Columns

Drag a field such as Other into the Columns area. The Pivot Table then displays that field across columns, with the values arranged under each column heading.
